name: First working transistor
short_desc: John Bardeen and Walter Brattain build a working transistor at Bell Labs, laying a foundation for modern electronics.
date_note: The device showed amplification on 16 December 1947 and was demonstrated to Bell Labs officials on 23 December. The public announcement followed in June 1948.
notes: Added after a catalog gap review on 24 October 2026. Supplies the missing hardware foundation between early computers and later personal-computing and web milestones. Evidence and date rationale: The point-contact device showed amplification on 16 December 1947 and was demonstrated to Bell Labs officials on 23 December. The public announcement came in June 1948; later junction and silicon transistors were separate developments. Primary evidence: https://www.computerhistory.org/siliconengine/invention-of-the-point-contact-transistor/. Cached Wikipedia introduction and lead image provide separately attributed background. Remains review, not comprehensive factual approval.
